title: World War I
summary: The Great War consumed a generation in mud and machine guns, reshaping borders and planting the seeds of an even deadlier conflict.

stories.title: The Western Front
stories.summary: From the Schlieffen Plan to the Armistice — five turning points in the war of attrition.

events.title: Invasion of Belgium
events.body: German armies swept through neutral Belgium en route to France. The violation of Belgian sovereignty brought Britain into the war and fixed the Western Front's northern anchor.

events.title: First Marne
events.body: Allied forces counter-attacked along the Marne and halted the German advance on Paris. The 'miracle of the Marne' ended hopes of a quick victory.

events.title: Verdun
events.body: Germany aimed to bleed France white at Verdun. Months of slaughter around the fortress became the symbol of industrialised attrition.

events.title: The Somme
events.body: British and French offensives on the Somme produced over a million casualties for minimal gain. The first day alone cost the British Army nearly 60,000 men.

events.title: Armistice
events.body: Allied pressure and internal collapse forced Germany to sign an armistice in a railway carriage at Compiègne. The guns fell silent at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day.

stories.title: The Eastern Front
stories.summary: The vast campaigns between Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Russia.

stories.title: War at Sea
stories.summary: Jutland, U-boats, and the blockade of Germany.
